title: Finite localized restriction maps detect boundary sections
statement: Let L be a locally Noetherian scheme, U an open, N a quasi-coherent module, V an affine open, and p a prime of R=O(V) whose point is outside U. For any submodule S of (j_*(N|U))(V), there exist finitely many R_p-modules Q_i, scalars a_i in the maximal ideal of R_p, and R_p-linear maps phi_i:S_p -> Q_i, such that multiplication by a_i is injective on Q_i and all phi_i(z)=0 implies z=0. The family may be empty.

proof.text: Local Noetherianity supplies QuasiCompact U.ι. The compact preimage of V has compact image U intersect V. Apply the fully proved source-library IsAffineOpen.exists_finset_basicOpen_eq and enumerate its finset by Fin s.card. Each chosen f_i lies in p: otherwise fromSpec(p) belongs to D(f_i), contained in U, contradicting the boundary hypothesis.

Let F=j_*(N|U) and let T_i be F(D(f_i)) with scalars restricted to R=O(V). Define g_i:S -> T_i by inclusion followed by restriction. On the open subscheme U, the preimages of D(f_i) cover the preimage of V. TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq' applied to N|U shows that g_i jointly detect zero. The structure-sheaf theorem isUnit_res_basicOpen makes multiplication by f_i injective on T_i. These are ordinary section modules; no quasi-coherence or affine localization identification is used.

Set Q_i=LocalizedModule.AtPrime p T_i and a_i=algebraMap(f_i), which belongs to the maximal ideal by IsLocalization.AtPrime.map_eq_maximalIdeal and Ideal.mem_map_of_mem. Define phi_i using IsLocalizedModule.mapExtendScalars. Localizing the injective endomorphism f_i times identity proves injectivity of multiplication by a_i, using IsLocalizedModule.map_injective and linearMap_ext.

For joint zero detection, represent z as m/d by mk'_surjective. map_mk' and eq_zero_iff give, for every i, a denominator c_i outside p annihilating g_i(m). The private common_annihilator lemma multiplies these denominators by induction on the finite set, including its empty case c=1. Linearity and joint detection imply c*m=0; mk'_eq_zero' now gives z=0. The private localized_joint_zero lemma contains this complete argument.

lean.statement:
theorem boundary_localized_finite_detector
    {L : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian L] (U : L.Opens) (N : L.Modules)
    (hqc : N.IsQuasicoherent) (V : L.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (S : Submodule (L.presheaf.obj (op V))
      (((Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj
        ((Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj N)).val.obj (op V)))
    (p : Ideal (L.presheaf.obj (op V))) [p.IsPrime]
    (hy : hV.fromSpec ⟨p, inferInstance⟩ ∉ U) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (Q : Fin n → ModuleCat.{u} (Localization.AtPrime p))
      (a : Fin n → IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
      (φ : (i : Fin n) → LocalizedModule.AtPrime p S →ₗ[Localization.AtPrime p] Q i),
      (∀ i, Function.Injective (fun x : Q i ↦ (a i : Localization.AtPrime p) • x)) ∧
      (∀ z, (∀ i, φ i z = 0) → z = 0)
